question_or_symptom: A memfd can have the expected byte size and ordinary permission bits while still carrying unsafe special mode bits, wrong access, mutable seals, extra links, or unexpected ownership.
observation: Checking only mode 0777 accepts setuid, setgid, or sticky bits. Checking only file contents ignores writable mappings and size-changing races that can invalidate CRC and caller-buffer atomicity.
conclusion: A carrier is a compound kernel-object identity and policy, not merely a file descriptor containing bytes.
decision: Require a regular anonymous file with exact effective UID, link count zero, exact size, CLOEXEC, operation-specific access mode, and `(st_mode & 07777) == 0600`; require exact H2D and D2H seal states, classify writable-map EBUSY as unauthorized and ENOSPC as resource exhaustion, and reread immutable D2H bytes before ACK.
invalidated_assumptions: Masking st_mode with 0777 proves exact mode 0600.
A matching length and CRC before final sealing makes D2H immutable.
